title: Stream warmup + credential-lease adapter: unify ergonomic iterators across SDKs
author: Asha Patel
description:
Context: Users reported stream cold-start variance and awkward reauth race conditions across SDKs when long-lived streaming sessions are resumed behind resumable tokens. This PR introduces a lightweight credential-lease adapter plus a small ergonomic surface for 'stream warmup' hints so SDKs can coordinate an early KV-cache priming request and avoid repeated auth handoffs.
Motivation: reduce token-swap races, unify retry/backoff defaults for streaming, and provide a minimal cross-language adapter that keeps idiomatic iterators in each SDK.
Summary of changes: - Introduce a credential lease abstraction (lease Adapter) in sdk/common that exposes RenewableLease interface and a small HTTP handshake for short-lived session leases. - Python: add redwood.session.lease.LeaseClient, a small context manager used by the async stream iterator to pin token leases for the duration of a resumed stream; add stream_warmup hint to StreamingClient.start_stream. - TypeScript: add compact StreamWarmupHint and a thin LeaseProvider shim that conforms to existing token provider types; add tests covering abort semantics. - Go: add adapter.go implementing the LeaseProvider for go-sdk, update stream iterator to accept WarmupHint and lease token context. - Backoff: add a 'streaming-warmup' preset in sdk/common/backoff with conservative initial window and jitter tuned for streaming heartbeats. - Docs: new markdown guide docs/sdk/stream-warmup.md and example in examples/stream-warmup. - Tests: end-to-end integration tests for streaming warmup in python/ts and unit tests for lease renewal edge cases.
Commits (high level): - 1a2b3c4: implement common lease contract and basic shim - 2b3c4d5: python LeaseClient + iterator integration + unit tests - 3c4d5e6: typescript lease provider + stream warmup hint - 4d5e6f7: go adapter + iterator changes + go tests - 5e6f7g8: docs, examples, and changelogs - 6f7g8h9: fix CI flake, adjust backoff timing
Motivation and rollout plan: This change is backwards compatible for all current token providers. The LeaseAdapter is optional: if no lease provider is supplied, SDKs fall back to existing token-refresh behavior. We will ship with an opt-in flag in the console for a small set of internal customers for two weeks, monitor stream error rates and auth exchange traces, and then flip the default.
Review conversation (abridged): - Miguel: "Nice overall shape. Two asks: please add a changelog entry per SDK and shrink the LeaseClient constructor surface for Python." - Asha: "Added changelog entries and tightened constructor; also added an example in examples/stream-warmup to show the minimal pattern." - Lena: "Can you add a test that simulates a failing renewal and ensures the iterator surfaces a RetryableStreamError?" - Asha: "Added test (tests/python/test_stream_warmup.py) and returned a RetryableStreamError with clear message; updated TS test accordingly." - Ravi (approval): "Verified E2E with dedicated infra - warmup reduced first-response latency variance by ~18% in our synthetic trace."
CI notes: Initial CI run: lint passed; python unit matrix had a flaky test (test_stream_backpressure) failing intermittently due to a timing assumption; addressed by replacing time.sleep with event-driven synchronization. Re-run CI: all checks passed (lint, unit, integration, e2e-smoke).
Files of interest (high level): - sdk/common/credentials/lease_adapter.go: core lease contract and a small HTTP handshake client. - sdk/python/redwood/session/lease.py: LeaseClient implementation and context manager used by async iterator. - sdk/typescript/src/stream/iterator.ts: new optional warmupHint param on startStream and LeaseProvider shim. - sdk/go/stream/adapter.go: Go lease adapter and small helper to thread context.Context for lease lifecycle.
Backward compatibility and breaking changes: none; all new surfaces are optional and fall back to existing behavior when unused.
Semantic version bumps: python SDK -> 2.1.0 (minor), typescript SDK -> 1.8.0 (minor), go SDK -> v0.12.3 (minor).
Release notes: "Introduce optional streaming warmup and credential-lease adapter to reduce stream cold-start variance and make cross-SDK streaming auth more robust. Opt-in for two weeks before flipping default for GA."
Merge outcome: merged via squash-and-merge after approvals from reviewers.
Follow-ups planned: - ENG-7310: rollout monitor and alert on stream auth error rate - ENG-7321: telemetry: add metric for lease-renew failures and warmup-success ratio - cleanup: consider collapsing token provider interfaces after broader adoption
Risk/mitigation: The only notable risk is over-reliance on the lease handshake adding a small constant (<5ms) to stream establishment; mitigated by the warmup hint which allows a parallel priming request that overlaps with existing connection setup. Internal testing showed net latency variance improvements for bursty workloads.
release_notes: Introduce optional streaming warmup and credential-lease adapter. Adds LeaseClient (Python), LeaseProvider (TS), and adapter for Go. Minor SDK bumps: py 2.1.0, ts 1.8.0, go v0.12.3. Opt-in rollout, monitor auth metrics.
